note: The Fatimid Caliphate claimed the title of rightful caliphs against the Abbasids; the Sunni-Shia divide expressed as a geopolitical rivalry between Cairo and Baghdad, with both powers sponsoring missionaries and proxy rulers across the Islamic world.

_quarry.structural_significance: Competing caliphal legitimacy claims fragmented Islamic political unity into Sunni and Shia spheres; the Fatimid counter-caliphate in Cairo forced every Muslim ruler to choose sides, undermining the fiction of a single Islamic commonwealth and establishing the sectarian divide that shaped Islamic political geography through the Crusader period.
